client_brief:
Nordhaven: signature image set

Project overview
Nordhaven is a fourteen-room hotel inside a converted brick and timber warehouse on the working harbour. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Nordhaven signature image set and Amenity cut-outs for the booking page.

What we will provide
nordhaven_property_shoot/ (16 frames, 4,200 to 5,000px long edge); nordhaven_amenity_objects/ (3 frames, 4,600px); nordhaven_brand_notes.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Additional archive files
nordhaven_room_card_2025.pdf; nordhaven_rooms.csv. These files are supplied for provenance only because their former deliverable class is outside this commission. Do not silently turn them into extra scope.

Scope and deliverables
- Nordhaven signature image set: The property shoot brought from two separate visits onto one base and then carried to a single committed tone with one tint hue, one strength and one grain across the whole set, plus the one true-colour room hero for the booking page held deliberately out...
- Amenity cut-outs for the booking page: The carafe, the robe and the key fob as genuinely transparent artwork whose edges hold on the near-black ground the booking page uses, judged on that ground rather than on white, with no edge bitten away where object and ground share value and no enclosed...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$900-$2,400 fixed; target delivery 7 to 15 business days; one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-22. This id carries an EMPTY real_brief_anchors array in the ledger, so there is no marketplace grounding note to quote and none is invented here. The anchor is the ledger concept itself, quoted verbatim: one_line_ask, 'Give our micro design-hotel a distinctive, moody signature image treatment for the lookbook and social, a single stylized tone that runs across every amenity and detail shot so it looks unmistakably like us and nothing like a generic booking listing'; price_demo, 'A design-led micro-hotel at $600/night for design-literate 30-45 urban travellers who choose on aesthetic; a committed, restrained monochromatic signature is load-bearing.' The verdict is REBUILD because that concept, as banked, ended in one tinted image set plus crops of it, which is one deliverable and one surface. The fuller commission a property in this position actually buys, and the shape these jobs are posted in on the freelance marketplaces (a launch kit rather than a retouch), is the one built here: the signature committed across a shoot that happened on two different visits, the amenity objects cut out for the near-black booking page, the lookbook and social canvases handed back editable because the room list changes, and the desk room-directory cards reprinted off last season's press file against a new rate sheet. The hotel is the fictional Nordhaven, in a converted harbour warehouse; no real property, platform, brand or person is referenced.

The hotel is the fictional Nordhaven, in a converted harbour warehouse; no real property, platform, brand or person is referenced.
price_band_and_audience: Design-led micro-hotel, six hundred dollars a night, sold direct to design-literate 30 to 45 urban travellers who choose a property on aesthetic and book it because it looks like nowhere else. The band is load-bearing on nearly every decision in the job. At this level a committed, restrained, near-monochromatic signature is the product: the guest is buying atmosphere and a point of view, so the treatment has to be strong enough to survive being seen three pictures at a time in someone's feed. Run the same commission for a one hundred and twenty dollar highway property and every choice inverts: that booker needs bright, literal, reassuring colour and a clear picture of the bed, and this moody tint would actively lose them. The band also decides where the tone stops. The one true-colour room hero exists because a guest paying this much wants to see the actual linen, and an agent that tints it for consistency has followed the pattern and broken the commission. The same restraint governs the collateral: air, one photograph doing the work, type that does not shout, rates set quietly rather than as offers. Cheerful, saturated, discount-shaped design at this price reads as a property pretending to be something it is not. The ledger records the base treatment at 400 to 900 dollars; this full launch commission, with the cut-outs, the editable canvases and the fourteen-record card run, sits at 1,400 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: A room with the harbour in it
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen-room design-led micro-hotel in a converted harbour warehouse, sold direct.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opened 2023 on the Nordhavn waterfront, Copenhagen; fourteen rooms run by one small owner-led team.
brand_identity.about: Nordhaven is a fourteen-room hotel inside a converted brick and timber warehouse on the working harbour. We sell the feeling of the building: cold light, plaster, oak and brass. Guests choose us because the place looks like nowhere else, and everything we make has to carry that.
brand_identity.audience: Design-literate urban travellers, 30 to 45, who choose a property on aesthetic and book direct once they trust the point of view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Six hundred dollars a night, direct only, positioned above the travel-platform grid as a design destination rather than a room count.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high-contrast serif for display, set large and used sparingly, with a clean neutral grotesque for text. Nothing shouts, and rates sit small.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, understated, first person, no exclamation. Example line: 'Fourteen rooms on the water. We open direct booking this autumn.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We work from a short brand note that fixes the near-black ground, the placements and the delivered sizes. There is no full guideline system yet, and the room list changes each season.
brand_identity.values: One committed tone across everything, with the true-colour main room photograph kept as the single deliberate exception so guests see the actual bed and linen.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_property_shoot/ (16 frames, 4,200 to 5,000px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Amenity and detail shots plus the rooms, from two visits, one in autumn and one in winter. They do not match." Bath and bedside details, the breakfast counter, the stair, the harbour window, plus one full-frame room.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody in the hotel can see. First, two of the detail frames separate their subject from their ground almost entirely by hue rather than by value (a moss-green wool throw lying on an oak-grey bench, a terracotta cup on a rust-red tray), so any single tone ramp collapses both of them into one flat field, while each still looks plausible on its own at thumbnail size. Second, the winter visit was shot after the blinds were replaced, so those six frames sit a step darker in the shadows than the autumn ones and plug solid once a tint is committed on top of an uncorrected base.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_amenity_objects/ (3 frames, 4,600px)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The carafe, the folded robe and the brass key fob, shot on our own surfaces so they would look at home." One object per frame, styled on the hotel's plaster and oak.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The unglazed carafe is photographed against the hotel's own limewashed plaster and its shadow side sits at almost exactly the plaster's value, so an automatic knockout succeeds, returns a clean-looking file, and quietly bites the lip and the shoulder away on that side. The key fob is the opposite problem: its plate carries an enclosed cut-out letterform that a background removal cannot punch at all, so that route returns the hole filled with captured oak while reporting success.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_room_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's room directory card, the file the printer used." A real press PDF of a single-sided card carrying the room name, the floor and bed line, the view line and the nightly rate, printed and font-embedded.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things the printed page does not reveal. The card's copy was set around the shortest room name the hotel had last year, so the name frame has very little slack at the merged type size, and InDesign does not spill an over-long merged record, it simply stops rendering it at the frame edge with no warning anywhere. And the four visual blocks on the printed card do not correspond to four converted frames: the conversion's real granularity is a property of how the PDF was drawn, not of how the card looks.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_rooms.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The fourteen rooms with name, floor, bed type, view line, nightly rate and an image column naming the frame each card should carry.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the fourteen rooms were renamed this season and now carry two-word names roughly half again as long as anything on last year's card, and their view lines are longer again. The rate column is also inconsistently typed across the rows, which is a copy decision the agent has to make rather than a defect any tool reports.

assets_supplied.name: nordhaven_brand_notes.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The near-black ground the booking page and the lookbook cover use, the placements and the delivered size each one is used at, the price band and who books, and the note that the main room photograph on the booking page stays true colour.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the committed tone actually does to this particular set. A single tone ramp maps every colour in a frame onto one hue, so any frame whose subject is told apart from its ground by hue rather than by value loses that separation completely. Two of these detail frames are exactly that case (a moss-green throw on an oak-grey bench, a terracotta cup on a rust-red tray) and both collapse into one flat field. Nothing in either photograph announces it: they look like ordinary detail shots, they look correct in colour, the tint operation reports success, and each tinted file still reads as plausibly moody on its own at thumbnail size. The collapse only exists as a comparison against the rest of the set at reproduction size. The strength that carries the other frames is also the strength that kills these two, so there is no single setting that resolves it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it: which frames depend on hue for separation is a property of what was in the room that day, and it cannot be read off a colour preview, since in colour both frames separate perfectly well. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for one tone across every amenity and detail shot and names the single true-colour exception it already knows about; it says nothing about any frame failing, and no asset note or earlier step identifies these two. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to go back before the tint and build luminance separation that was never there, by lifting or dropping one side under a mask, or to accept that these two frames are not treatable and change which frames carry which pages.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the corrected base for those frames and separate subject from ground by value under a mask before re-committing the tone, then re-tint and look at the set again rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the frames that were not flagged at the same reproduction size, since the reason to look was found on two frames and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not separate without looking manipulated, drop it and re-plan the lookbook around the frames that survive.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The lookbook opens on two grey mush frames in the middle of a set that is supposed to be the property's entire point of difference, and they go out on the social canvases as well, in front of exactly the design-literate booker the direct-booking channel was built to reach.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs hold where they are actually used. The carafe is unglazed and was styled against the hotel's own limewashed plaster, so on its shadow side the object and the ground sit at effectively the same value. The knockout succeeds, returns a clean-looking transparent file, and has quietly taken the lip and part of the shoulder with it. On white and on any pale layout that missing edge is invisible, because what is gone was pale anyway; on the near-black booking ground it reads as a bite out of the silhouette. Which of the three objects does this, and how far the bite runs, is a property of the styling in that one photograph rather than of the route chosen or the care taken, and no tool reports edge quality at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it: the cut-outs have to be made regardless of sequence, there is no metadata that describes an edge, and the defect does not exist in the returned file in isolation, only in relation to the ground it is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The client says every version they tried looks fine until it goes on the dark, which is a client describing the symptom that made them hire somebody, not a statement of which object, why, or that the cause is a shared value on one side. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is a different operation on a different principle, selecting the plaster as a material and inverting rather than asking for the object, and it carries a further decision about whether the object needs restyling advice back to the client rather than a cut.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected object by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the subject, re-composite on the near-black ground and inspect the same edge again rather than assuming the second route worked, and inspect the other two objects at the same magnification, since one object having been caught is not evidence about the others. If an edge cannot be recovered, say so and propose the object be reshot on a ground that separates, rather than shipping a bitten silhouette.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The booking page, the one page the entire launch exists to convert on, carries a carafe with a chunk missing from its side, which is the precise defect the client hired someone to fix, handed back as fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fourteen merged cards are actually complete at trim. Last season's card was set around the shortest room name the hotel had, and three rooms were renamed this season with longer names and longer view lines. A merged record that exceeds its frame does not spill, does not wrap onto the card and does not raise anything: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the card comes back looking like a properly composed card that happens to name a room slightly differently. Every automatic signal passes: the merge reports success, the page count equals the row count, the pages are in the printer's order and each card carries the correct room photograph. The frame's true capacity at the merged type size is not published anywhere and cannot be computed from the printed card, so the only way to know is to merge and look at all fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot pre-empt it: capacity depends on the frame geometry the conversion produced and the type size the template carries, neither of which is knowable before the merge exists, and comparing string lengths against last year's copy gives no threshold. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the room list changes and hands over a spreadsheet with the new rates and views, which is a client describing their content, not disclosing that three records overrun. No asset note in the client's hands names the rooms and no acceptance line explains the cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a decision the client has to be involved in, shorten the copy, move the long field to a frame that can hold it, or change the type treatment on the card, and each of those changes the mapping and the design rather than repeating an operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which records are cut, decide with the copy in hand whether the fix is an editorial shortening, a re-mapping so the long field lands in a frame with slack, or a type change on the card, then rebuild the mapping, re-confirm the placeholders in the round-tripped document, re-merge and look at all fourteen again rather than only the three that were caught.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen room cards go to the printer and sit on the desks of a hotel that charges six hundred a night with three of them naming the room half way through a word, discovered by guests rather than by anyone at the hotel.

decision_gates: Which single frame is the true-colour exception, and holding it out of the treatment when the headline ask is consistency.
How far the tone is pushed, given that at this band restraint is the design and the same strength that carries most frames destroys the ones that separate by hue.
Whether both visits are brought onto one base before the style is committed, or the style is committed on top of two different bases.
Where a global correction stops working and the move has to be masked to a named material rather than to the object sitting on it.
Whether a frame that collapses under the tone is rescued by building value separation or dropped from the set, and which page then carries which picture.
Knockout route per object rather than per batch, given that one of the three cannot be knocked out by background removal at all.
On which ground the cut-out edges are judged, when both failure modes are invisible on white.
Whether to extend a frame at its edges or accept a tighter crop, knowing extended material has to match the tone that was already committed.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a hotel that does not exist. IDENTITY is the commission: these are sixteen frames of one specific building, one specific carafe and one specific brass fob, and the entire direct-booking proposition is that the guest is seeing this property rather than a generic mood. A regenerated interior is a misrepresentation on a booking page, which is a legal problem and not only a craft one. SPEC: the deliverables are defined by surfaces and numbers a generation cannot satisfy, genuine partial-alpha transparency that survives on a named near-black ground, crops composed at named delivered sizes with no output larger than its source, and fourteen cards at one record per page in the printer's order carrying the correct room's photograph. EDITABILITY: the lookbook set exists as a deliverable because the client edits it themselves as the room list changes, so it has to arrive as a native document with live text and real photographs, not as a flat picture of a layout. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this frame still separate once the tone is committed, does this edge hold on the ground it will actually sit on, does this record still fit its frame at trim. None of that is a generation problem, and none of it can be checked by looking at a render.
